generations.prompt:
Two pictures come with this request.

IMAGE 1 is the picture you edit: the lower part of a frame of our own rhythm game's play screen. Note lanes run away from the camera, a glowing aqua judge line crosses them, under it lies a row of eight glossy key caps (white ones and aqua-blue ones), and under that row, between the two white side rails (each with an aqua line inside and a pink line outside), lies the gear's lower panel: a wide slab that runs from the key caps down to the bottom edge of the image, widening toward the camera. In image 1 the panel is a FLAT LAYOUT DRAWING of a console: a dark teal pane with thin rings round its middle; at the middle a white ring-shaped mark, three curved arrows chasing one another round a pale disc, in an aqua glow; at each side five slanting aqua stripes (a vent) over a long white bar (a blade); white armour plates in the two far corners, right under the key caps; hot-pink triangles at the outer edges and pink hatch stripes in the two near corners. The drawing shows exactly where each thing lies and how large it is.

IMAGE 2 is the DESIGN REFERENCE: a small concept picture of this very console (it is enlarged, so it is blurry), in the style the panel must have: the cockpit console of a clean white machine with aqua lights and hot-pink accents: gloss-white armour with cut corners, a dark teal glass pane with a soft aqua glow at its middle, the machine's mark (a white ring with three small arrow heads round a glowing pale core), aqua vent stripes, pink trims. Match its design language, its colours and its mark. Its two rows of number boxes (MAX COMBO, SCORE) are NOT wanted: leave them out, and write no text at all.

Keep image 1's framing EXACTLY: the same camera, the same zoom, the same crop; your picture must overlay image 1 pixel for pixel, so the judge line, the row of key caps and the two side rails stay at exactly the same places and sizes. Do not zoom in, do not crop, do not widen, do not recompose, do not enlarge or shrink the panel. Repaint ONLY the panel: the area under the row of key caps, between the inner edges of the two side rails, down to the bottom edge of the image. Keep every other pixel exactly as it is: the lanes, the notes, the judge line and the splash on it, the row of key caps, the rails, the dark background.

The panel becomes that console as a photorealistic 3D render at the finish of a commercial console game, seen exactly from this camera. Every thing of the layout drawing stays exactly at its place and at its size (the same footprint, the same angle), foreshortened by the camera exactly as in image 1: do not move, enlarge or shrink anything, do not stand anything upright, and add nothing.

1. THE WATER: in this version the console's field is not glass but WATER: a shallow pool of clear aqua water over a deep teal bed, held between the white armour, lit from underneath at its middle so that it glows aqua there and deepens to dark teal toward the edges. Its surface is alive: round ripples go out from the mark in rings (the drawn rings), each a soft swell that catches a bright line of light, widening and fading toward the edges; a few small round drops and tiny bubbles lie on the surface (about where the drawing has its small pale dots). Real, clear, calm water, with soft reflections of the white armour in it.

2. THE MARK, at the middle: the machine's mark of image 2 as a solid thing: a thick ring of gloss-white ceramic armour split into three arcs that chase one another, each ending in a small arrow head (as drawn), floating flat at the middle of the pool, just above the surface, and mirrored softly in the water under it; the ripples start from it. Inside the ring, a round lens of pale aqua glass that glows from within: the machine's core, bright, soft and clean. A halo of aqua light lies on the water round the mark.

3. THE VENTS, at each side: the five slanting stripes of the drawing are five louvre slats cut into the console, each glowing aqua from inside, the outermost the brightest and the others fainter toward the middle.

4. THE BLADES, under each vent: a long, slim blade of gloss-white armour (as drawn, its inner end cut at a slant), raised a little, with a fine line of aqua light along its upper edge.

5. THE ARMOUR, in the two far corners right under the key caps: plates of gloss-white ceramic armour with cut corners (as drawn), about as thick as a finger, with a few fine panel lines, two or three small flush bolts each, and a thin line of aqua light along their inner edge. The narrow white strips at the two near sides are the same armour.

6. THE PINK: the triangles at the outer edges and the hatch stripes in the two near corners (as drawn) are inlays of glossy hot-pink enamel, flush with the surface; the thin aqua lines beside the hatch stripes are fine lines of light.

Each raised thing throws a soft shadow. Clean, bright, crisp and new: no dirt, no scratches, no wear. The top edge of the panel under the key caps is a thin bevelled lip. Everything stays inside the rails; nothing rises over the rails or above the key caps, and the panel runs on down past the bottom edge of the image (no front edge is seen). Nothing else is on the panel: no screens, no number boxes, no buttons, no knobs, no cables, no people, no hands.

No text, letters or numbers anywhere, no logos, no watermark, and nothing over the lanes. Colours: gloss white; deep teal; aqua light (close to #22E0E6); hot pink (close to #FF3F93).
